props.gloss_en: the mishna's 'one who traps them for a need is liable' -- who taught it? it is R' Shimon
R' Shimon: for a labour not needed for its own sake, one is exempt
one who lances an abscess on Shabbat to make an opening for it is liable
...to draw out fluid from it, he is exempt
who taught [the abscess ruling]? Rav Yehuda in Rav's name: it is R' Shimon
one who traps a snake on Shabbat, busying himself with it so that it will not bite him, is exempt
who taught [the snake ruling]? Rav Yehuda in Rav's name: it is R' Shimon
Shmuel: one who takes a fish out of the sea is liable once [an area] the size of a sela on it has dried
R' Yosei bar Avin: and [the dried area is] between its fins
Rav Ashi: do not say actually dry, but even where it forms slime
Shmuel: one who reached into an animal's innards and detached the fetus in its womb is liable
Rav Sheshet: one who detaches hops from shrubs and thorns is liable on account of uprooting a thing from its place of growth
here too [the fetus], he is liable on account of uprooting a thing from its place of growth
Abaye: one who detaches a mushroom from the handle of a jug is liable on account of uprooting a thing from its place of growth
one who detaches from a perforated pot is liable
...and from one that is not perforated, he is exempt
there [an unperforated pot] that is not its growth; here [the jug handle] that is its growth
